title: Amplification for proper base-change squares
statement:
Let $\square$ be the cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] with
$X,Y,X',Y'$ noetherian of finite dimension, $f$ and $f'$ proper, and suppose
there is a positive integer $N$ annihilating $A/I$ which is invertible on
all four schemes. Assume that the geometric fibers of $f$ have dimension at
most $e\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$. Then
$$
 \mathrm{AMP}(\square;2e),\qquad\mathrm{WIT}(\square),\qquad\mathrm{TOW}(\square)
$$
of [def-weil-pbc-finite-level-amplification],
[def-weil-pbc-witness-compatibility] and [def-weil-pbc-tower-preservation]
all hold.

are the proper finiteness theorem of SGA 4 1/2, whose Stacks amplitude form
is Lemma 59.92.2 ([Tag 095U](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/095U):
$R^qf_*=0$ for $q>2n$ and abelian torsion coefficients, all fibres of
dimension $\le n$) and whose compact-support form is Theorem 63.14.5 ([Tag
0GL0](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0GL0): constructibility of
$Rf_!K$ for $K\in D^+_{tors,c}$), together with Definition 61.29.1 ([Tag
09C1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C1)), Proposition 61.29.7 ([Tag
09C7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C7)) and the reduction-tower
bounds of Lemma 61.29.2 ([Tag
09C2](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C2)); the blueprint adds the
simultaneous assertion of $\mathrm{AMP}$, $\mathrm{WIT}$ and $\mathrm{TOW}$
for a proper square with fibres of dimension at most $e$.

proof.text: Fix the adic datum $(A,I)$ and put $P_n=A/I^n$. Evaluating $N(A/I)=0$ on $1$ gives $N\in I$, so $N^n\in I^n$ annihilates $P_n$; a power of a unit is a unit on all four schemes. To check the fibre bound for $f'$, use that proper implies locally finite type. The fibre-dimension base-change statement [lem-sc-fibre-dimension-after-base-change], applied also to geometric residue-field extensions, identifies its local fibre dimensions with those of $f$. Taking their supremum by [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions] gives the same bound $e$. Empty fibres contribute $-\infty$ and cause no exception.

source.place: Proof (a), annihilators and base-change fibre bound

proof.text: Apply [thm-weil-pbc-direct-image-finiteness-proper] to $f$ and $f'$ at every $P_n$, using the torsion annihilator and fibre bound just verified. This supplies both FIN clauses with the same $2e$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-preserves-bounded-constructible] to $g$ and $g'$ for exact triangulated pullback and preservation of every cohomological interval. These are precisely the two clauses of [def-weil-pbc-finite-level-amplification], proving $\mathrm{AMP}(\square;2e)$.

Every finite-level bounded constructible object admits an etale witness by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Normalization morphisms lift uniquely between witnesses by the full faithfulness in [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]. Tensor comparison identifies their source with the pulled-back etale derived reduction; exactness and conservativity on etale sheaves in [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level] ensure that this reduction is bounded whenever the supplied pro-etale normalization makes it bounded. For $u=f$ or $f'$, put $B=P_{n+1}$, $C=P_n$. For a compatible witness $K_{n+1}\cong\nu_U^*L_{n+1}$, use the proper torsion projection formula [lem-kun-0f0g] over $B$ with the constant coefficient complex $C$. It gives $(Ru_{\mathrm{et},*}L_{n+1})\otimes^L_B C\cong Ru_{\mathrm{et},*}(L_{n+1}\otimes^L_B C)$. The comparison [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image] identifies its two ends with the corresponding pro-etale direct images; choose the specified canonical exchange isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate], whose counit normalization is exactly the exchange used by the tensor-coherence lemma. Tensor commutes with $\nu^*$ by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]; [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence], applied to the comparison square of topoi, says these identifications commute with the projection map. Thus the transported witness and its normalization are the same on both routes. This proves normalization and witness compatibility for both direct images. Properness gives the qcqs hypothesis of the comparison theorem via the scheme conventions. No perfectness of $C$ as a $B$-module is used.

source.place: Proof (b), direct-image normalization and witnesses; corrected projection-formula argument

proof.text: For $u=g$ or $g'$, derived inverse image commutes with tensor by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Apply this with the constant quotient $P_n$ to pull the supplied normalization $K_{n+1}\otimes^L_{P_{n+1}}P_n\cong K_n$ to the normalization of $Lu^*K_\bullet$. The comparison isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] transports the etale witnesses. On a K-flat representative the normalization is the balancing map $(x\otimes b)\otimes c\mapsto x\otimes q(b)c$; inverse image applies to this same formula. For three quotients either order sends $((x\otimes d)\otimes b)\otimes c$ to $x\otimes q(d)q(b)c$. Hence quotient cocycles and witness compatibilities agree. Together with the preceding direct-image step this is $\mathrm{WIT}(\square)$ of [def-weil-pbc-witness-compatibility].

Let $M_\bullet$ be any uniformly bounded constructible input tower, with local terms supported in $[d_0,d_1]$ as in [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-tower]. By [lem-weil-pbc-uniform-perfect-quotient-bound] choose one $r$ with all $P_n$ represented in $[-r,0]$ by finite projectives over $A$. The flat constant-to-completed coefficient comparison [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] gives the same bound over the completed coefficient sheaf. Tensor the local bounded complex with these resolutions: each reduction is supported in $[d_0-r,d_1]$, uniformly in $n$. Its finite-lisse cohomology on the supplied finite stratification is intrinsically constructible by [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf]. Apply the etale-origin conclusion of [lem-weil-pbc-normalized-constructible-local-effectivity] to this normalized input tower with the interval just proved: it belongs to the etale-origin bounded constructible category at every level. This bridge is necessary because the definition of that category uses etale origin, not only intrinsic constructible cohomology. By AMP and [prop-weil-pbc-amplification-consequences], the two direct-image output levels are constructible in $[d_0-r,d_1+2e]$ and the two finite pullback output levels are constructible in $[d_0-r,d_1]$.

source.place: Proof (c), uniform bounds on all input and output levels

proof.text: These finite-level outputs are the evaluations of the strict-tower functors in TOW. For direct image this is [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits]. For completed-coefficient tower pullback, use the objectwise K-flat construction [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] and the flatness and finite-quotient identities of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]. Write $R=\underline A$, $B=u^{-1}A_T$, $B'=A_{T'}$, $S_n=(P_n)_{T'}$. Flatness and $B\otimes^L_R S_n\cong S_n$, $B'\otimes^L_R S_n\cong S_n$ give $B'\otimes^L_B S_n\cong S_n$ by derived tensor reassociation [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Consequently, for any supplied $R_n$-level object $M_n$, $B'\otimes^L_B u^{-1}\operatorname{Res}M_n\cong\operatorname{Res}(u_n^{-1}M_n)$; this is not an identification of the two ambient coefficient categories. Naturality in $M_n$ makes the isomorphisms commute with all transitions. The preceding normalization arguments supply quotient-coefficient level structures, inducing the actual transitions, with the quotient cocycle. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-normalized-constructible-local-effectivity] to each output strict tower with the common interval from the preceding step. It supplies one finite stratification and common bounded adic-lisse finite-type local complexes, with reduction maps compatible with normalization. Thus the full data required by [def-weil-pbc-tower-preservation] exist for each of the four functors on every input tower. This proves TOW, and completes all three assertions.

split_report.summary: Expanded AMP, normalization and witness transport, uniform finite coefficient bounds, strict tower evaluations, and local effectivity. Corrected the false perfectness assertion over P_{n+1}; reused the proper torsion projection formula. Added three strictly smaller statement-only tools, not functor-preservation restatements.

tool_uses.why: Generic proper torsion projection formula, valid for arbitrary torsion rings, supplies coefficient normalization; no theorem of this unit gives the nonperfect quotient case.
Generic local fibre dimension under base change; the input is proper and hence locally finite type.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $\square$ be the cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] with
$X,Y,X',Y'$ noetherian of finite dimension, $f$ and $f'$ proper, and suppose
there is a positive integer $N$ annihilating $A/I$ which is invertible on
all four schemes. Assume that the geometric fibers of $f$ have dimension at
most $e\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$. Then
$$
 \mathrm{AMP}(\square;2e),\qquad\mathrm{WIT}(\square),\qquad\mathrm{TOW}(\square)
$$
of [def-weil-pbc-finite-level-amplification],
[def-weil-pbc-witness-compatibility] and [def-weil-pbc-tower-preservation]
all hold.

proof.text:
*step (a), AMP.* In the quotient datum of the adic coefficient datum, the
condition $N(A/I)=0$ means $N\in I$. Hence $N^nP_n=0$, and $N^n$ is
invertible on the four schemes for every $n\geq1$. The geometric fibers of
$f'$ are base changes of those of $f$, hence of dimension at most $e$, so
[thm-weil-pbc-direct-image-finiteness-proper] gives
$\mathrm{FIN}(f,P_n;2e)$ and $\mathrm{FIN}(f',P_n;2e)$ for every $n\geq1$,
i.e. clause (i) of [def-weil-pbc-finite-level-amplification]; clause (ii) is
[lem-weil-pbc-pullback-preserves-bounded-constructible] for the two
pullbacks.

*step (b), WIT.* The finite-level functors commute with the normalization
isomorphisms for $P_{n+1}\to P_n$: for the direct images this is the
projection-formula compatibility of the reduction maps (the tensor with the
perfect $P_n$ commuting with $Rf_{*,n+1}$), and for the pullbacks it is the
tensor compatibility of inverse image with the quotient maps. A compatible
etale-origin witness [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]
$K_n\cong\nu_X^*L_n$ is transported: for the direct images by
$$
 Rf_{*,n}K_n\cong Rf_{*,n}\nu_X^*L_n\cong\nu_Y^*Rf_{\Et,*}L_n
$$
of [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image] (the quotient tower being built
from the same $L_n$), and for the pullbacks by
[lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]; the compatibility of the transported
witnesses is the above commutation with the normalizations. Hence
$\mathrm{WIT}(\square)$.

*step (c), TOW.* A uniformly bounded constructible tower is compatibly
witnessed on the local models $L_{\alpha j}$ supported in $[d_0,d_1]$ with
finite lisse cohomology reductions, and step (b) transports the witnesses.
The levelwise direct images are therefore etale-origin; their reduction
cohomology is bounded constructible by
[thm-weil-pbc-direct-image-finiteness-proper] with the amplitude containment
of [prop-weil-pbc-amplification-consequences], and the local models are
obtained from the etale-origin descriptions: a finite lisse module is finite
locally constant, which is exactly what the tower condition requires, while
no freeness is needed or available, a finite module over a finite local ring
being possibly non-free (for instance $\mathbf Z/2$ over $\mathbf Z/4$). The
pullback side is [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-preserves-bounded-constructible].
The output tower is hence uniformly bounded constructible, i.e.
$\mathrm{TOW}(\square)$.

The source text records that audit item BC-07 was resolved by correcting the
definition rather than the proof: the bounded constructible tower and the
tower-preservation condition formerly required the local models to have
finite locally *free* terms, which a general constructible complex does not
have. The requirement is now finite local constancy, which is exactly what
finite lissity gives.
